title: Canonical naive cotangent complexes commute with filtered algebra colimits
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $J$ a small filtered category, $j\mapsto S_j$ a diagram of commutative $R$-algebras, and $(S,(\iota_j))$ a colimit cocone in commutative $R$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For each $R$-algebra $T$ form its canonical two-term naive cotangent complex $N(T)=\mathrm{NL}_{T/R}=[I_T/I_T^2\to\bigoplus_{t\in T}T\,\mathrm d[t]]$, $I_T=\ker(R[T]\to T)$, in degrees $-1,0$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], and regard it as a complex of $R$-modules by restriction of scalars. For an $R$-algebra map $u:T\to T'$, let $u_\sharp:R[T]\to R[T']$ fix $R$ and send $[t]$ to $[u(t)]$; use the canonical chain map $N(u)$ given by $[f]\mapsto[u_\sharp(f)]$ in degree $-1$ and $a\,\mathrm d[t]\mapsto u(a)\,\mathrm d[u(t)]$ in degree $0$. Let $K$ be the degreewise colimit in $R$-modules of the diagram of these two-term complexes, with its induced differential. Then the canonical comparison chain map $c:K\to N(S)$ characterized by $c\circ\eta_j=N(\iota_j)$, where $\eta_j:N(S_j)\to K$ are the colimit maps, is a quasi-isomorphism; thus $Q(c):Q(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(N(S))$ is an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(R))$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. No transition map is assumed injective or flat, and no finite-presentation hypothesis on the algebras is imposed.

source.place: Tag 07BQ (lemma-colimits-NL), constant-base specialization, expressed as the canonical derived comparison after restricting scalars to R; the same finite-data assertion for a small filtered category rather than a directed set.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise] to regard $S$ as the colimit of the underlying rings. By [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise], elements have representatives and equality is witnessed at a common later object. In particular, for two elements at the same stage the two witnessing arrows can be made equal by filteredness, giving a single arrow witnessing their equality. We will make finitely many choices simultaneously: repeatedly choose common targets for the finitely many stages, and then equalize the finitely many parallel arrows that occur, using the definition in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Previously obtained equations persist under further maps. This proves the finite bookkeeping needed below without replacing $J$ by a directed set.

source.place: Tag 07BQ (lemma-colimits-NL), proof; explicit constant-base filtered-category finite-data argument

proof.text: Put $P_j=R[S_j]$ and $P=R[S]$, with polynomial maps given by renaming variables. These maps exhibit $P$ as a colimit of the $P_j$ in commutative $R$-algebras. Indeed, for a compatible family $h_j:P_j\to C$, assign to $s=\iota_j(t)$ the value $h_j([t])$. If two representatives give the same $s$, the common-target equality from step 1 and compatibility of the $h_j$ show that the assigned values agree. The polynomial universal property [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] extends this assignment uniquely to $h:P\to C$. Its composites with $P_j\to P$ agree with $h_j$ on every variable and on $R$, hence agree everywhere. Uniqueness follows since every variable of $P$ has a representative. This is exactly the colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Tag 07BQ (lemma-colimits-NL), proof; explicit constant-base filtered-category finite-data argument

proof.text: Write $I_j=\ker(P_j\to S_j)$ and $I=\ker(P\to S)$. Evaluation commutes with renaming, so each $I_j$ maps into $I$. Every $f\in I$ comes from some $f_j\in P_j$: apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise] to the polynomial colimit of step 2. The evaluation of $f_j$ maps to zero in $S$, so step 1, using [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise] for the $S_j$, gives one arrow $j\to k$ where that evaluation becomes zero. The image $f_k$ therefore belongs to $I_k$ and still represents $f$. Thus every element of $I$ is the image of an element of one $I_k$, not merely a sum of such images. Apply [lem-sfb-filtered-colimit-conormal-modules] with this polynomial diagram and these ideals. Its hypotheses have just been verified, and it gives the colimit cocone $I/I^2$ with precisely the maps $[f_j]\mapsto[(\iota_j)_\sharp(f_j)]$. By uniqueness of module colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], the component $c^{-1}:K^{-1}\to I/I^2$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 07BQ (lemma-colimits-NL), proof; explicit constant-base filtered-category finite-data argument

proof.text: Put $F_j=\bigoplus_{t\in S_j}S_j\,\mathrm d[t]$ and $F=\bigoplus_{s\in S}S\,\mathrm d[s]$. The prescribed maps form an $R$-linear cocone. Every element of $F$ is a finite sum $\sum a_r\mathrm d[s_r]$; lift its coefficients and labels to one stage by step 1, proving surjectivity on representatives. Suppose $v=\sum_{t\in E}a_t\mathrm d[t]\in F_j$, with finite $E\subset S_j$, maps to zero. Partition $E$ by equality of $\iota_j(t)$. In each part choose a label. Step 1 makes all labels in that part equal at one later stage, simultaneously for the finitely many parts. For each part $B$, the coefficient sum $\sum_{t\in B}a_t$ has zero image in $S$, since it is the coefficient of its common label in the zero image of $v$. Step 1 kills all these sums at one further stage. There $v$ is zero, because its terms within each part have the same label and their coefficients sum to zero. The colimit criterion [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-criterion] now applies to the $F_j$ and $F$, giving that $c^0:K^0\to F$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 07BQ (lemma-colimits-NL), proof; explicit constant-base filtered-category finite-data argument

proof.text: Check compatibility with the differentials, including variable collisions. For $u:T\to T'$, define $D_u:R[T]\to\bigoplus_{t'\in T'}T'\,\mathrm d[t']$ by applying $u$ to the coefficients of $\delta_T$ and sending $\mathrm d[t]$ to $\mathrm d[u(t)]$. Both $D_u(f)$ and $\delta_{T'}(u_\sharp(f))$ vanish on $R$, send $[t]$ to $\mathrm d[u(t)]$, and satisfy the Leibniz identity with coefficients evaluated by $u\circ\gamma_T$. Expanding a polynomial as a finite sum of monomials and applying the product rule factor by factor therefore makes them equal. If distinct labels have the same image, their terms add on both sides. This calculation is the explicit formula for the differential in [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]; it also shows that $I_T^2$ maps to zero and that the induced conormal and free-module maps commute with the differential. Renaming and coefficient maps preserve identities and compositions on representatives. Thus the two component colimit comparisons are the components of the canonical chain map $c$ specified in the statement.

source.place: Tag 07BQ (lemma-colimits-NL), proof; explicit constant-base filtered-category finite-data argument

proof.text: The components in degrees $-1$ and $0$ are isomorphisms by steps 3 and 4, and all other components are maps between zero modules. Their inverses commute with the differentials: multiply $c^0d_K=d_Nc^{-1}$ by the two inverse component maps. Hence they give an inverse chain map to $c$. The induced maps on kernels, images and their quotients are then mutually inverse in every degree, so $c$ is a quasi-isomorphism by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The localization $Q$ in that same definition inverts $c$, giving the asserted isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(R))$.

The item is not superseded: live and side-live both have it unsplit, the new id is absent from both, and there is no re-split note. The statement, stmt_deps, source and blueprint match live, and the citer lem-sfb-ind-etale-naive-cotangent-acyclic uses exactly the stated K→NL_{S/R} quasi-isomorphism in R-modules. Steps checked against the statements they cite. Step 1: representatives and common-target equality, with the filtered equalizer making the two witnessing arrows into one. Step 2: polynomial colimit, with the assigned value well defined across representatives. Step 3: f∈I lifts to f_j and one arrow makes γ_k f_k=0, since evaluation commutes with renaming; all hypotheses of the new node hold and its maps are the degree −1 components of N(ι_j). Step 4: free-module colimit via the modules criterion, partitioning the support by image; tested with R[x]→R, where the labels x and 0 merge. Step 5: Leibniz comparison of D_u with δ∘u_♯, with no false claim that partial derivatives commute with renaming. Step 6: a degreewise iso is a quasi-isomorphism, inverted by Q. New node lem-sfb-filtered-colimit-conormal-modules is true: an element whose image lies in I² gets its finitely many factors lifted, and ring-colimit equality puts it in I_m² at a later stage. Tested on single-object J, zero ideals, unit ideals and Z[x]→Z, where the class of x dies. It is self-contained, statement-only, sourced to 07BQ and not a restatement of the item. The duplicate search (07BQ, conormal∧colimit, naive cotangent∧filtered; directed-union-cotangent-h1, locally-dense-cotangent-h1, colimit-etale/unramified, finite-stage relations) found none, and the four kinds of Mathlib search found no match. No tool_uses: every off-unit citation is a Mathlib leaf or a definition. No changes.

lean.statement: theorem filteredColimit_comparison {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {J : Type (max u v)} [SmallCategory J] [IsFiltered J] (F : J ⥤ CommAlgCat.{max u v} R) (c : Cocone F) (hc : IsColimit c) (k : Cocone (F ⋙ functor R)) (hk : ∀ n : ℤ, IsColimit ((HomologicalComplex.eval (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) (.up ℤ) n).mapCocone k)) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{max u v} R)] : QuasiIso (comparison F c k hk) ∧ IsIso (DerivedCategory.Q.map (comparison F c k hk))
lean.note: The comparison is canonical IsColimit.desc from an arbitrary degreewise colimit cocone. Both QuasiIso(c) and IsIso(Q.map c) are stated. The fixed-base functor is supplied by the accompanying definition node. No flatness, injectivity or finite-presentation hypothesis occurs.
